section_summary: This section documents United States and Allied policy concerning food supply, collections, and civilian rationing in occupied Japan between December 1947 and July 1948. It encompasses Far Eastern Commission policy decisions and diplomatic correspondence transmitting Directive Serial No. 88 to General MacArthur, an article from The Economist examining the economic and political tensions between Japanese farmers and urban consumers, and State Department clearance memoranda regarding a proposal to increase livestock production. The remainder consists of a major joint report by General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), evaluating staple food production, emergency collection programs, distribution deficits, and the public health impact of acute food shortages and malnutrition during the second year of the occupation.

subfiles.about: Transmits a draft directive on food supply for civilian consumption in Japan and related statements by Allied representatives to SANACC for forwarding to General MacArthur via the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
subfiles.from: Frank G. Wisner, Deputy to the Assistant Secretary for Occupied Areas
subfiles.summary: Memorandum forwarding a draft directive based on a Far Eastern Commission policy decision of December 11, 1947, to the Joint Chiefs of Staff for transmission to General MacArthur. Encloses statements by the United States representative on November 20, 1947, and by the United States, Chinese, and New Zealand representatives on December 11, 1947, regarding minimum civilian food import requirements and reparations issues. The New Zealand statement emphasizes the suffering of countries devastated by Japanese aggression and urges that food imports to Japan be kept strictly to the minimum required for the safety of occupation forces.
subfiles.title: Draft Directive Regarding the Supply of Food for Civilian Consumption in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a certified copy of Directive Serial No. 88 to SCAP regarding civilian food supply in Japan for filing with the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: C. V. Hulick (for Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Transmits a certified copy of Directive Serial No. 88 to SCAP for filing with the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Certified Copy of Directive, Serial No. 88, to SCAP Regarding Supply of Food for Civilian Consumption in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of Directive Serial No. 88 to SCAP, implementing the Far Eastern Commission policy decision on the supply of food for civilian consumption in Japan.
subfiles.from: W. A. Schulgen, Acting Secretary, State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Committee
subfiles.summary: Transmits four copies of Directive Serial No. 88, which instructs SCAP to ensure maximum Japanese food production, maintain equitable rationing and price controls, and limit 1947–1948 food imports to the minimum necessary to prevent disease and unrest endangering occupation forces.
subfiles.title: Directive Transmitted to SCAP by the Joint Chiefs of Staff (Serial No. 88)

subfiles.about: Transmits an article from The Economist by G. F. Hudson examining Japan's post-war food crisis, urban-rural tensions, and political repercussions.
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, First Secretary of Embassy, London
subfiles.summary: Transmits an article by G. F. Hudson analyzing Japan's food crisis resulting from population growth, loss of colonies, and industrial collapse. The article discusses peasant resistance to official grain collections, black-market sales, political clashes in the Katayama cabinet, and the need for American aid to stabilize democracy.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 131: Transmitting Article from Economist on Food and Politics in Japan

subfiles.about: Provides drafting suggestions on an attached letter regarding Mr. Nozu's proposal for expanding Japanese livestock production.
subfiles.from: John M. Allison, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.summary: Provides drafting suggestions on a letter regarding Mr. Nozu's proposal for increasing Japanese livestock production.
subfiles.title: Clearance of Attached Letter

subfiles.about: Confirms that the letter concerning livestock production has been cleared and retyped incorporating NA's suggested modifications.
subfiles.summary: Confirms clearance and retyping of the letter incorporating NA's drafting suggestions.
subfiles.title: Clearance of Attached Letter

subfiles.about: Transmits a comprehensive SCAP joint report reviewing food production, collection quotas, distribution, imports, and nutrition in Japan during the second year of occupation.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo (J. D. Edwards)
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmitting a comprehensive joint GHQ SCAP report assessing Japan's food situation during the 1946–1947 occupation year. The report examines staple crop yields, emergency quota collection enforcement, rationing targets, and distribution deficits across prefectures. It highlights the indispensable role of American food imports in averting urban starvation and documents chronic malnutrition, caloric shortfalls, and declining labor output among the Japanese population.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 395: Food Situation in Japan During Second Year of Occupation
